correctness.rationale: PASS: Euclidean projection onto any oriented-tree isotonic cone is continuous, piecewise affine, with each active connected block replaced by the average of its input values. Every connected forest partition occurs on an open strict-complementarity KKT region since the oriented quotient of a tree is a DAG and the active incidence rows are independent. The edge-cut indicator functions form an exact l1 variation basis modulo constants; therefore a block-average map has TV norm equal to the largest image of a single cut. If the split edge lies in an active block S, its two sides of sizes a,b have output boundary jumps (b*p+a*q)/(a+b), and otherwise gain 1. This proves the global max formula and local attainment. Rooted side tree-knapsack obtains the exact rational maxima in polynomial time. Paths give 1; stars max(1,(m-1)/2); spine-plus-pendant cubic caterpillars yield k/2. Independently enumerated 19 families of finite trees with rational cut formulas, consistent with these sharp cases. Proof covers all finite oriented trees, not merely the samples.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: isotonic projection and graph total variation are established objects, but located sources on convex isotonic fitting and TV denoising do not provide this unweighted Euclidean isotonic-projector two-input graph-TV operator norm, its all-tree cut-boundary sharpness formula, or the bounded-degree unbounded-amplification caterpillar.
